title: Alkene Structure and Isomers Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A zip locks two sides, a ladder with two rails cannot twist and a double knot will not turn. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 9, Hydrocarbons) Diya sees raw bananas ripen faster next to ripe ones, thanks to ethene, and we learn the structure, isomerism and preparation of alkenes.

On the molecule bench, two sp2 carbons overlap head on for the sigma bond, then their p orbitals overlap side by side for the pi bond (C=C 134 pm, 681 kJ/mol against C-C 154 pm, 348 kJ/mol). Twist one carbon and the pi overlap drops to zero, so the double bond cannot rotate. Then structural isomers of C4H8, cis and trans but-2-ene, four ways to make alkenes link by link with curved arrows (Lindlar's catalyst, dehydrohalogenation, dehalogenation with zinc, acidic dehydration), a worked example with 1,2-dibromopropane and zinc, cis vs trans from but-2-yne with dipole moments, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 92 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:

2:28 Four ways to make alkenes, link by link
3:28 Worked example: 1,2-dibromopropane + zinc
4:04 Lindlar vs sodium in liquid ammonia
